subject: Banking
title: Small Business Lending Fees
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Small Business Lending Fees.

hook.text: Small business loans charge 6-13% interest plus origination fees of 1-5%. A $100,000 loan costs $5,000 just to open.

buildup.text: Banks consider small businesses risky. Higher rates and fees compensate for the chance the business fails.

discovery.text: SBA-guaranteed loans reduce bank risk. The government covers 75-85% of losses, yet banks still charge full rates.

twist.text: Big banks approve only 13% of small business loan requests. Community banks approve 49%.

climax.text: Small business lending is high-margin, high-risk. Banks profit from fees and rates that reflect risk they've often.

punchline.text: High rates plus fees plus government guarantees. Banks profit while risk shifts.

quiz.question: What approval rate do big banks have for small business loans?
